採用・広告の製品.quote: Didge Construction Robots for Progress and Safety

Didge transforms the way construction teams manage projects by delivering continuous, real-time site digitization. It provides real-time, ground-truth facts, enables a proactive approach to construction management that prevents costly mistakes before they happen.

It can mitigate risks and predict issues. The result is a boost in workforce productivity, stronger risk management, and increased profits. Didge autonomous robots capture high-frequency, high-fidelity live site data from which Didge AI instantly processes ground-truth facts, prioritizing them based on urgency.

It combines all mission-critical applications on one platform. By autonomously capturing and analyzing massive volumes of site data from multiple angles, Didge creates insights that previously were impossible to generate, provides a holistic and unbiased view of project state.

These insights are delivered to the teams through automated reports, alerts, and interactive dashboards, ensuring immediate action. Didge enables fully and infinitely scalable Construction Intelligence. It is the key to a radically new approach to construction management that directly addresses the core challenges of modern construction.
Jobsite Progress Precisely Tracked by AI

Didge helps project managers stay ahead of schedule and eliminates expensive project delays. It automatically calculates work-in-place percentages for all trades. AI-driven analysis detects slowdowns before they escalate, flagging areas at risk of delay.
With seamless visibility into subcontractor performance and production rates, teams can verify billing, optimize coordination meetings, - reducing disputes and keeping projects on schedule.

Didge provides an immediate reduction in the number and severity of jobsite incidents. Didge reinvents construction safety by making risk detection proactive, and unbiased - based on the ground-truth facts and AI. AI continuously monitors jobsite conditions, identifying flags hazards and unsafe behaviors in real time.

These insights create a feedback loop for the crew, enabling the teams to immediately correct unsafe behaviors, rectify hazards, and prevent incidents. High-risk behaviors are significantly reduced within weeks from the Didge deployment.
Disciplined data collection for best AI and human insights. Precisely capture your entire jobsite area every day with
unprecedented quality

Didge provides easy-to-use tools for the teams. Progress, safety, and quality reports are generated automatically and can be customized to include the metrics stakeholders care about most. All the issues can be tracked on the Didge platform shared directly within Procore, Autodesk, Oracle products, or other project management tools.

It creates a holistic data representation of the project – ensuring all stakeholders have a shared source of truth. Didge eliminates miscommunication and delays – bringing facts, validating assumptions, and increasing the speed of decision-making.

Didge spots quality issues early, prevents expensive rework and delays. It provides an unprecedented level of visibility into installation quality across every phase of construction. AI systematically inspects installed components, checking for deviations from design, code violations, and conflicts.

Any issues are flagged on the Didge platform and automatically posted into standard field management tools. By identifying quality concerns early, Didge helps projects avoid expensive delays and corrective work.

“Utilizing Didge felt like doubling our site team. It took a lot of repetitive work out of the people's hands so we could focus on building - getting things done faster, preventing mistakes from happening and making more informed decisions. As a result, we're three months ahead of schedule – with zero extra lift for the team".
— RYAN SPOTTS, SR. PROJECT EXECUTIVE

“The time saved by using Didge is pretty remarkable. Ordinarily, a team member would spend hours weekly manually taking pictures. With Didge, we never have to worry about someone forgetting to take a picture or skipping a day, these robots never take a day off!”
Experience AI-powered project management without the hassle of manual data collection
Book Didge for your project, today.

Do you know what the biggest cause stopping the evolution of AI is right now? It is not the programming technology of the latest models, nor is it a shortage of genius researchers. The answer is "electricity" and "heat."
In other words, no matter how smart an AI program you develop, if you do not have the "electricity" to run it and the "cooling mechanism" to keep it cool, it will just be an inert box.

This is precisely why long-established electrical and infrastructure companies like Siemens are becoming the unsung protagonists of the AI boom.

Construction sites change shape every day, with the placement of materials and the progress of work shifting moment by moment. Until now, humans have had to walk around the site to check progress and ensure there are no anomalies.

• Reduced human waste: The robot's eyes (sensors) will detect mistakes and rework early, such as "workers waiting even though materials haven't arrived" or "pillars being erected in the wrong position compared to the blueprints."
• Accurate data retention: Site conditions are digitized in real-time every day, allowing for an accurate grasp of the situation even from a remote location.

Rather than immediately replacing humans with complex construction tasks, this is a very smart approach that advances automation starting with the steady and reliable step of "first accurately grasping the site situation."

Until now, it has been in the academic research stage of "can such a thing really be built?" However, what this news means is that we have finally entered the practical phase of "how to incorporate the completed technology into business and society."

Cutting-edge technology cannot be completed by a single company or a single country. Japan and Australia are joining forces to begin building a cross-border "quantum technology utilization network" while training researchers and engineers.

Until now, the mainstream for AI has been a 'Q&A' format where humans input questions and receive answers. Recently, however, it has evolved into 'AI agents' (AI that performs tasks on its own)—where you provide a goal, and the AI thinks of the steps, searches the internet, compiles documents, and sends emails.
As more companies begin to seriously use these AI agents in business settings, a new problem has emerged.
The system that AWS has started providing this time is, so to speak, a 'strict registry and storage shelf exclusively for internal AI agents.'
The four news items covered this time have one clear commonality. It is that 'the battlefield has shifted from discussions about digital software to physical and operational real-world problems.'
